Wear thick pants! The concrete is unforgiving if you don't have enough cardboard. Great view from the top too.
Unbelievable amount of wood carvings hidden in the trees. It feels like a fantasy world right next to the noisy BART tracks.
The highest point in the city but so few people here. The eucalyptus forest is magical in the fog, and the cross is massive up close.
On a jetty in San Francisco Bay, the Wave Organ is a unique acoustic sculpture designed to amplify the natural sounds of the bay's waves.

Mt Davidson is a scenic and quaint getaway from the buzzing streets of SF. Dramatic panoramic views in every direction. On a clear day, you can see far the hills of the faraway south bay and diablo area.
A true hidden gem in Pleasanton. The grounds are impeccably kept and it's a peaceful spot for a walk or history lesson.
Great photography spot. The old buildings and the butterfly garden provide excellent backdrops.
Surprisingly scenic and educational. The Murray Schoolhouse exhibit is very well done and explains the local history perfectly.
Hidden in plain sight. Most people drive right past it, but it’s a lovely place for a picnic and a step back in time.
The best views in the Tri-Valley, hands down. It's much quieter than the main Ridge entrance.
A local secret. The trails are steep but the payoff at the top is incredible. Make sure you check the entry requirements first!
Charming and nostalgic. My kids loved seeing the old tractors and the big Victorian house is beautiful.
A wonderful piece of history. The docents are very knowledgeable and the atmosphere is very relaxing.
An incredible piece of art that looks like paper but is massive steel. Truly a hidden wonder in the middle of a business district.
Hard to find if you aren't looking for it, but definitely worth the photo op. The detail of the 'folds' is impressive.

locationName: Mandalay Canal Walk at Las Colinas
comment: It feels like you’ve been transported to Europe. It was wonderous to see the Canal Walk lit up at night!

locationName: Mandalay Canal Walk at Las Colinas
comment: A peaceful escape from the workday stress. Great for a romantic stroll or just a quiet place to think.
Excellent tour. The clever projection vignettes throughout the home go far in bringing the riveting story to life.
A must-see for any Kennedy assassination enthusiast. TheTalking dioramas made it even more immersive.
Love the steamed momos and chow mein. Great halal option and truly authentic flavor!
Don't let the location fool you. This is some of the best Nepalese food in the country. The jhol momo is a must-try.
Amazing place to walk around with beautiful scenery and night vibes. Definitely a must see if you are in the area.
So peaceful. Walking alongside the canal or riding the gondola makes you understand why this is a hidden gem.
A perfect place to get away from the hustle and bustle of the city. This trail is a beautifully maintained paved pathway.
This is a really nice park! There's an area where you can actually play in the fields so bring your dogs out.
Great spot for a quiet walk by the river and some history about the pioneers. Very untouched feel compared to other city parks.
Good for biking and hiking. It feels like you're deep in the woods even though you're right near Las Colinas.
Most people just see the horses and leave, but the museum inside the towers explains the incredible detail and history of how they were made. Well worth the visit.
A quiet, informative spot. The staff are very knowledgeable and the story of the artist's journey to Kenya and Spain is captivating.
Nice little trail for something so nearby. Carrollton has done a very good job with the preserve. It's quiet and perfect for a quick morning hike.
I've hiked this twice. Great for a morning run or walking with kids who want to read the nameplates describing the local trees.
A little gem hidden away in Coppell. The stonework from the 30s is still beautiful and the history of Sam Houston camping here is fascinating.
Beautifully maintained with lots of shade. It’s not a major trail system, but it's the best spot for a peaceful afternoon walk.
Amazing facility that teaches you about local flora and fauna. The building itself is a work of art with its solar panels and rainwater collection.
A hidden educational treasure for families. The nature walks led by docents are top-notch and very informative for kids.
Amazing experience. The owner is super nice and you must try their onion rings. It feels like stepping back into the 1950s.
Loved the decor! Every town has a special place where people gather, and this is definitely Coppell's spot for great breakfast and company.
An incredible tribute to Audie Murphy. The cotton history section was surprisingly fascinating, and the WWI trench exhibit is very immersive.
A true hidden gem for aviation enthusiasts. The collection of vintage drones is one-of-a-kind, and the family that runs it is incredibly knowledgeable.
The most unique theater experience I've had. It feels like a private show in someone's very fancy living room. The food and the sound quality are top-notch.
The banana split chocolates are amazing. It's a great place to stop for gifts and a taste of local history that you can't find elsewhere.

locationName: In-Sync Exotics Wildlife Rescue and Educational Center
comment: An incredible experience. You can tell the staff truly loves these animals. It's much more intimate and educational than a typical zoo.

locationName: In-Sync Exotics Wildlife Rescue and Educational Center
comment: Great place to spend an afternoon. The cats look happy and well-cared for. A hidden treasure in Wylie!

locationName: Olde City Park & The Burnett House
comment: The Victorian house is beautiful and the park is so peaceful. It’s a great spot to take photos and learn a bit about local history.

locationName: Olde City Park & The Burnett House
comment: Quaint little park right off the main street. Very clean and well-maintained. A nice break from the suburban sprawl.
The atmosphere here is wonderful. They have a great selection of Texas wines and the staff is very knowledgeable.
Perfect date night spot. The chocolate-dipped wine is a must-try. So glad we found this spot in downtown Wylie!
One of the best parks in the area. The trail system is great for running and the amphitheater is a beautiful spot for events.
Beautiful park with plenty of space. The playground is excellent and the pond area is very serene.
Ridiculously delicious and healthy too! The flavors are unique and the service is incredibly warm.
Inlay Tea Leaf Salad is as refreshing as a spring breeze and incredibly flavorful. Kouswe is fantastic as well.
A perfect neighborhood spot for a date night. Great variety of wines and the charcuterie board was top-tier.
Friendly staff and a very helpful wine selection. The atmosphere is relaxed and classy.
LLELA is a beautiful, clean, and excellent park to hike and photograph. A true escape from the city feel.
Great place for kayaking on the Elm Fork. You feel like you're miles away from civilization.
The best tacos in the area and a craft beer list that puts most bars to shame. Don't let the strip mall location fool you.
Authentic flavors and super friendly owners. The Al Pastor is a must-try!
A hidden treasure. Once you get past the golf course, you feel like you are in a national park. The views at the tip of the peninsula are incredible.
Very peaceful and clean. Just make sure to apply sunscreen as parts of the trail have limited shade.
One of the coolest interiors I've seen in a coffee shop. The ambiance is perfect for relaxing or catching up with friends.
Love the vintage vibe and the local feel. It's a must-visit destination in downtown Lewisville.
Absolutely incredible view during sunset. It's safe, peaceful, and one of my favorite places to unwind in nature.
A great place for a picnic and photos. The wooden deck is huge and offers sweeping views of the water.
This park is such a hidden gem! The cliffs make the views stunning, and it's the perfect place for both adventure and relaxation.
The best spot in the DFW area to watch the sunset. The rocky shore makes you feel like you aren't in Texas anymore.
An inspirational walk you won't soon forget. Thousands of unique rocks with beautiful messages and characters.
My kids spent hours looking at all the different designs. It is such a creative and peaceful use of a nature trail.

locationName: Grapevine Botanical Gardens at Heritage Park
comment: A small parcel of peace and respite. I love finding hidden gems like this that are free and so well-maintained.

locationName: Grapevine Botanical Gardens at Heritage Park
comment: Beautiful, quiet place for a stroll. The water features are very soothing and the plants are labeled for learning.
Step back in time! It’s amazing to see a working farm preserved so well right in the middle of the city.
Great for kids to see the sheep and chickens. The farmhouse tours are very informative about early Texas settlers.

locationName: Bob Jones Nature Center and Preserve
comment: An absolute oasis. The trails are well-marked and the history of Bob Jones is inspiring. Great for bird watching.

locationName: Bob Jones Nature Center and Preserve
comment: Hidden gem in Southlake. The Bluebird Trail is perfect for a quick walk with great views of the lake area.
Very moving tribute. The symbolism of the crew members facing the directions of the lost flights is powerful. Quiet and respectful.
A must-visit. It's a small park but incredibly impactful, especially with the planes flying overhead.
Watching the artists work is mesmerizing. We did the help-create event and it was the highlight of our trip!
Unique experience and the gallery has some stunning pieces. Highly recommend the seasonal ornament making.
Absolutely stunning rock formations. It doesn't even feel like you're in Flower Mound once you get down into the creek bed.
Great spot for kids to explore the rocks, though it can get a bit muddy after the rain. A true hidden diamond in the suburbs.
A very spiritual and quiet place. The wildflowers in the spring are breathtaking, and the view of the sunset is one of the best in town.
Simple, short walk but very peaceful. It's a miracle this hasn't been developed into houses.
